title: Trigger point
description: A named trigger point (model/trigger-points/): what runs when one of its verbs happens to an object whose entity its subjects cover, with or without a lifecycle. Its body is a lifecycle's trigger point's, without the keys that belong to one lifecycle (states, targets and transitions). At each moment it runs before the lifecycles' trigger points.

name.description: An identifier, unique among the named trigger points of the package (MQ3001); a refusal names it.

subjects.description: The types it runs for, at least one: an entity, with the entities derived from it, or a stereotype, standing for every entity that carries it and the entities derived from them. Removing the last one removes the trigger point, since an empty list would run it everywhere.

exceptEntities.description: Entities it skips, each with its derived entities, though a subject covers them: the opt-out, written where the rule is. Each must be one a subject covers (MQ8102).

entities.description: Entities it runs for, each with its derived entities: some of those its subjects cover (MQ8102). Empty: every entity its subjects cover, less exceptEntities. Its paths and sets name what every entity it covers holds under one id.

when.description: It runs only when this is true; false or unknown skips it, and the trace says so. It reads the object under subject, its values before the verb under old, current_actor(), in_state (a state of any lifecycle) and now(); never the context or an event's payload (MQ3102).

description.description: Why. For a check, the message shown when it refuses or warns; without one, the display name, else the name.

rationale.description: Markdown text: why the element is shaped this way.

decision.description: A URL or a reference (such as ADR-0042) of the decision record. It is not an element id and is not checked.

excludeStereotypes.description: Stereotype keys that a database schema's or a package's defaultStereotypes would give this element, left out with the stereotypes they imply. Only defaults can be excluded (MQ2029).

subject.title: Subject
subject.description: A type a named trigger point runs for: an entity, with the entities derived from it; or a stereotype, standing for every entity that carries it and the entities derived from them. Names exactly one of entity and stereotype.

entity.description: The entity. Not written together with stereotype.

stereotype.description: The key of a stereotype that applies to entities (MQ2003, MQ9211): it covers every entity that carries it (package defaults, implied stereotypes and its own list, less what it excludes) and every entity derived from one. Not written together with entity.
